Name: Shane Ryoo
Question: What are ways to self study to learn equal to the knowledge in a major, as in the way you can save tuitions, and show on resume, then how could I prove my learning experience?
Answer: There is no “equal” way to learn at the same speed and quality as a good undergraduate program, and thus no proving anything. By self-studying: Can people learn better by themselves than from a bad teacher and fellow students? Sure: been there, done that. But in the aggregate, the only way you’re going to beat a full undergraduate education by yourself is by using a really crappy undergraduate program as your standard.

Name: Shane Ryoo
Question: Is it a good idea to get a bachelor's in biomedical engineering and then a master's in mechanical engineering?
Answer: No. It may be a bad idea because you won’t be allowed in many mechanical engineering graduate programs. You won’t have the prerequisite background. The other way around is a safer bet, but in engineering it’s generally better to stick to one engineering discipline and pick the handful of courses you need in adjacent areas as necessary, without worrying about those credentials.

Name: Shane Ryoo
Question: What are the most versatile bachelor’s degrees (like business administration/management) but without math?
Answer: The moment you cut out math, you’re so hamstrung, it’s a bit silly to talk about versatility. You might as well say, “If I’m missing an arm, what can I play in American football?” If you’re not American, the answer is “the kicker, some of the time.” Out of several dozen players. Business administration without math is garbage. How do you measure money or performance without math? Even some basic calculus is a useful tool, which is why it’s taught in top business programs.

Name: Shane Ryoo
Question: I have always gotten good grades (mostly A’s), but I never seem to be able to get any higher no matter how hard I try. I wish to rank in the top ten. Is there a problem with me?
Answer: It’s a “problem” if you haven’t admitted that your “wish” is a fantasy. Your question exhibits potential causes of your lack of performance relative to your “goal.” You say “top ten,” but ten of what exactly? Ten percent? Ten students (out of what size class)? You made an assumption that “top ten” means something to the rest of us. It does not. That kind of fuzzy thinking and communication is what causes mistakes. Multiple mistakes cause non A grades. Do you analyze every single mistake you make on homework and exams to figure out why you got it wrong and make sure that you don’t make the same mistake, or similar mistakes, ever again? If you’re not, then you’re not working very hard or very smart. You say you’re trying “hard,” but that’s a meaningless opinion. The fact that you’re of school age on Quora means your life is a lot easier than most of humanity’s. Are you working “harder” than those people? Probably not. Be more precise in your thinking, work smarter, work harder, and get off of Quora. Or admit that you’re not willing or able to operate at that level and give up on your wish.

Name: Shane Ryoo
Question: Is a PhD in computer science worth it financially?
Answer: For most people, compared to the alternatives, no. There are PhDs who are probably doing as well as if they didn’t do the PhD. Common characteristics I see: It begs the question of whether they would have done as well or better if they stopped at the master’s. I suspect most of them would have done just as well without the PhD, although industrial research would have been closed off to them. As I have said in many other answers, do not expect a graduate degree to “fix” anything regarding jobs. People should pursue PhDs to do the jobs that require a PhD. Those jobs (professor) may not have higher pay.
